messages:
acme_prod_owner: Hey team — since ~09:20 UTC our dedicated eu pool shows big latency spikes (70ms -> 2.1s) and a few 429s. Happens only on the gpt-small-prod route. No recent deploys on our side. Can you check noisy neighbor / MIG contention?

sam_support: Sorry about that — looking now. Can you drop a couple example request IDs? We'll correlate logs and metrics.

acme_prod_owner: Request IDs: r-20260317-11, r-20260317-14, r-20260317-19. Also saw one "CUDA out of memory" in the infra logs while running a synthetic batch test. We didn't change batch sizes.

metrics-bot: Node redwood-eu-dc3-07: GPU0 util 99%, memory_used 95%, sm_efficiency 98%. Dedicated pool eu-west spike at 09:20 UTC. Autoscaler activity: scaled +1 at 09:21 UTC.

maria_sre: I can see the same in infra metrics. One MIG partition (1g.5gb) shows persistent 100% SM utilization across multiple processes. Looks like a single tenant is saturating cycles.

jon_eng: Can you paste nvidia-smi query for that node? e.g.:
```
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.total,memory.used,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory --format=csv
```

acme_prod_owner: Pasting output snippet from the affected host:
```
index, name, memory.total [MiB], memory.used [MiB], utilization.gpu [%], utilization.memory [%]
0, A100-SXM4-40GB, 40960 MiB, 38800 MiB, 99 %, 94 %
(mig device 1g.5gb slices mapped, multiple pids showing heavy usage)
```

sam_support: That matches noisy neighbor behavior. Autoscaler adding nodes reduced pressure but root cause is intra-node sharing. We'll cordon the node and migrate slices off to reduce tail latency.

deploy-bot: autoscaler: scaled dedicated-eu by +1 at 1769991260 (reason: burst load).

maria_sre: Plan: 1) cordon redwood-eu-dc3-07, 2) drain MIG slices with low-priority tenants to other nodes, 3) throttle offending tenant via rate limit/cap. I'll run drain now.

jon_eng: Possible root cause — tenant launched a large synchronous batch job (batch_size=512, seq_len=2048) against a model compiled for full-GPU assumptions while running in a 1g.5gb MIG slice. That leads to aggressive SM scheduling and CUDA context pressure. Repro steps: run heavy-batch synthetic test against a 1g MIG slice and watch sm_efficiency climb to 95%+ and token latency jump.

acme_prod_owner: Appreciate the repro steps — we can try to reproduce locally and delay some large jobs. After cordon/evict, we saw tail latencies drop back toward baseline.

maria_sre: Actions taken: cordoned redwood-eu-dc3-07, drained lower-priority MIG slices, applied temporary token-rate cap for tenant 0x7b. We'll re-evaluate MIG partitioning profiles and add a smoke check so batch jobs aren't scheduled into small MIG slices.

sam_support: Follow-up items: - postmortem with timeline and mitigation steps, - recommend per-tenant GPU memory/cgroup enforcement, - add autoscaler preference to place new reserved workloads on emptier nodes. I'll open a support ticket and assign to eng-runtime for a fix. :white_check_mark:

acme_prod_owner: Thanks all — service looks stable now. Please keep us posted on permanent mitigations.

maria_sre: Noted. We'll include the repro commands and a suggested policy (disallow large-batch jobs on 1g MIG profiles) in the postmortem.

sam_support: Closing loop once PM and eng-runtime have signoff.
